messages:
lia-support: Customer reports repeated 400s from /v1/rerank after upgrading their client SDK. They say it started toggling after a deploy and affects ~20% of requests. Customer is on Dedicated plan so they're asking for a quick workaround and root cause. Attaching their exact body they sent.

samir-eng: can you paste the raw curl or body? helps repro locally.

lia-support: here is what customer pasted in the ticket (redacted api_key):
```json
{
  \"requestId\": \"acme-123\",
  \"payload\": {
    \"candidates\": [
      {"id": "a", "text": "first option", "score": "0.87"},
      {"id": "b", "text": "second option", "score": "0.65"},
    ],
    \"topK\": "3"
  },
}
```

lia-support: customer says server responded with 400 and message: "Invalid request body". They pasted no other headers.

samir-eng: TL;DR: I can repro. Two problems: 1) trailing commas in the JSON (after the second candidate & after root) => some parsers error out; 2) they wrapped candidates under payload and send topK as a string and scores as strings. Our rerank schema expects top-level `items` array (or `candidates` top-level per older SDK mappings), numeric `top_k` (or `topK` as number) and numeric scores if provided. The request fails in our validation layer before hitting ranking logic.

samir-eng: quick repro curl I used (note: I removed trailing commas):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer redacted" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"requestId":"acme-123","items":[{"id":"a","text":"first option","score":0.87},{"id":"b","text":"second option","score":0.65}],"top_k":3}'
```

rerank-bot: ValidationError: body.items must be an array of objects with keys [id,text] (received items under payload.candidates).

maria-se: Could this be caused by the new JS SDK auto-stringifying numeric fields? We shipped a change in 2.4.5 that coerces some form inputs to strings when serializing.

samir-eng: plausible. The payload the customer sent looks like an intermediate envelope (payload.candidates) — older clients did that. But our strict validator rejects non-top-level items. Also numeric-as-strings break schema. Both cause 400.

maria-se: For mitigation: 1) we can add a transient server-side tolerant path that accepts payload.candidates and coerces score/topK types (flag behind a config). 2) For immediate customer unblock, provide a small wrapper snippet to transform their body before sending.

lia-support: I sent the customer this workaround snippet and asked them to try. Also asked for their SDK version.

lia-support: workaround snippet sent: (they can run client-side before send)
```js
function normalizeRerankBody(body) {
  if (body.payload && Array.isArray(body.payload.candidates)) {
    body.items = body.payload.candidates.map(c => ({ id: c.id, text: c.text, score: Number(c.score) }));
    delete body.payload;
  }
  if (body.topK) body.top_k = Number(body.topK);
  return body;
}
```

samir-eng: For the engineering follow-up I opened GH issue #4478 to add a tolerant parser and a telemetry flag to measure how many clients send envelope payloads. Will link the issue in the ticket.

maria-se: also asked infra to check logs for that customer's org id to confirm rate and any auth anomalies. Lia, can you collect the example failing request id and paste it in the ticket?

lia-support: done — I added the failing request_id from logs and escalated to eng since customer is on Dedicated. Customer will test the normalize snippet and we requested SDK version.

maria-se: next steps: - engineering: decide if tolerant path goes behind runtime flag (samir: assign) - devex: patch SDK docs and call out serialization change in 2.4.5 - support: follow up with customer and keep escalation open until they confirm unblock

samir-eng: assigning GH #4478 to myself, will PR a tolerant handler + unit tests. If we see >5% of requests from active dedicated customers using envelope format we'll roll a temporary tolerant path.

lia-support: customer tried workaround and reported immediate success for 12/12 requests. Closing interim support loop; keeping eng escalation open for a durable fix. :thumbsup:
